# Inside the Nucleus

<!-- STEP id="proton" -->
## The Proton

The nucleus holds all the positive charge of an atom, and Rutherford showed that this charge comes from particles he named **protons** (symbol p⁺). A proton has a charge of +1, equal and opposite to the charge of -1 on an electron, and it is much heavier than an electron.

<!-- STEP id="balance" -->
## Protons and Electrons Balance

A whole atom has no overall charge, so the plus and the minus must add to zero. This means an atom always has the same number of electrons as protons. A helium atom has 2 of each, and a sodium atom, like the one in our grain of salt, has 11 of each.

<!-- STEP id="hydrogen" -->
## The Simplest Atom

Hydrogen is the simplest atom of all, with one proton and one electron. Almost all of its mass is that one proton.

So if helium has 2 protons, you can ask how heavy a helium atom should be. The answer showed that something was missing from this picture.
